category.description:
High-level category of the issue (e.g., 'queues', 'jobs', 'data', 'async-actions').
Dimension for grouping by issue type.

subcategory.description:
Specific subcategory within the category (e.g., 'action', 'calc', 'map-reduce').
Dimension for finer-grained grouping.

severity.description: Issue severity level - dimension for filtering and prioritization.

targetType.description:
Target type of the obj with the issue.
Dimension for grouping by affected type.

targetAction.description:
Action name in the `targetType` associated with the issue (for action/job-related issues).
Dimension for grouping by specific action of a target type.

targetField.description:
Field with the issue. If null, the issue applies to all fields in the `targetType`.
Dimension for identifying problematic fields.

targetId.description:
Id of obj with the issue. If null, the issue applies to all objs for the `targetType`.
Dimension for grouping issues by specific instance.

errorCode.description:
Primary error code categorizing the issue.
Dimension for grouping by error type.

acl.description: List of {@link AclEntry} entries governing who can read/update/remove Objs.

typeIdent.description:
Indicates explicit sub-type of entry.  Composed of the concatenation of the typeKey of the instance's type and all
of its base type's typeIdent

id.description:
A unique identifier that can be manually assigned or generated automatically during object creation. This
identifier cannot be altered after the object has been persisted.

version.description:
Version number used for optimistic concurrency.  Automatically managed by the system.

Updating an Obj with a null or 0 value for version will cause the concurrency check to be skipped and should only
be done with great caution.

typeWithBindings.description: Persists concrete type with bindings for generic types where instance has parameter bindings

summary.description: Human-readable summary of the message describing the issue.

message.description: Message produced by the system for this issue, should contain all the details, like error messages and call-stacks.

timestamp.description:
Timestamp when the issue was created or last updated.
Useful for tracking issue history and age.

title:
Base type for all application issues across queues, jobs, actions, and data.
Provides common fields and methods for issue tracking, categorization, and resolution.

Categories are extensible - applications can define their own. Common platform categories
include: 'queues', 'jobs', 'async-actions', 'data'.

Issues are stored in 'system' domain for option to enable:
- Centralized access e.g. from Studio for cross-app analytics
- Availability even when individual apps are down
- System-level monitoring and alerting

Note that by default `system` domain is hosted by the App and ACL for Issues is not enabled.

In order to store Issues in a remote system db first configure the Db.Domain to point to a remote app then
enable Access Control by creating:

1. `AclPrivilege` record:
   ```json
   {
     "id": "App.Issue_AclPrivilege",
     "typeName": "App.Issue",
     "canUpdate": "true",
     "canRemove": "true",
     "canModifyAcl": "true",
     "acl": { "expr": "_context.appId" }
   }
   ```

2. 'EnableAclPrivilege' record:
   ```json
   {
     "id": "App.Issue_EnableAclPrivilege",
     "enabled": true,
     "typeName": "App.Issue"
   }
   ```

See {@link AclEnabled} for more details on access control configuration.
name: App.Issue
